entries.site: aisef/control/gate.py::_nop_check (the `unrunnable and not test_format` branch; 'red or absent' at level 2) + aisef/phases/implement.py::run_nop (pytest collection interruption)
entries.semantic_context: the deterministic 'tests verify story' control — and TDD, which defers to it ('the nop control proves the same thing directly') — can PASS on tests that never executed at the parent SHA. (A) A nop run that failed because a third-party dependency is missing is recorded with `unrunnable` AND `test_format` (pytest printed its collection error); the gate's UNRUNNABLE branch requires `not test_format`, so it falls through and scores the absent tests as red: PASSED. The same record without test_format is UNRUNNABLE, as SS-26/INV-F.3 intend. (B) When one story test file fails to import at the parent (the legitimate red), pytest interrupts the whole session; the story's other test files never run, the kernel's parser reports no test ids, and 'red or absent' scores a tautological AC test (`assert True`) in another file as verified: PASSED.

entries.semantic_context: the detector that recognises 'the missing module is the story's own code' matches a module name against changed file stems, but has no package rule: `No module named 'ledgerlock'` does not match `ledgerlock/__init__.py`. A greenfield story's legitimate red at the parent is logged as 'control NOT performed' while the gate (via SS-81's path) scores the same record as proof — two kernel records disagree about one piece of evidence.

entries.semantic_context: TDD's 'red before green' accepts any non-ok test run as the red: a run that could not execute at all (unrunnable — tool/environment) and a run red only because an UNRELATED pre-existing test failed both make TDD PASS, although neither shows the story's tests failing without the story's code.

entries.semantic_context: a story that declares no criteria passes 'tests verify story' whenever the parent run is red for ANY reason — environment, collection, unrelated failures. Plan-time machine gate blocks zero-criteria plans, which is why this is P2, not P1.

entries.site: aisef/control/gate.py::_baseline_check (baseline unrunnable NO_SETUP branch; aborted collection)
entries.semantic_context: 'no baseline regression' passes vacuously when the baseline did not execute: a collection-aborted baseline yields no green ids, and a dependency-unrunnable baseline is read as 'no test was ever green there' — so an existing test the story deletes is never seen as lost.

entries.semantic_context: a test green at baseline and SKIPPED at the candidate is neither 'red' nor 'lost' to R9, so a story can silence an existing test with a skip marker and 'no baseline regression' passes.

entries.semantic_context: on Windows, concurrent memory writers are intermittently refused with 'memory path escapes project': safe_path compares Path.resolve() of _bmad-output/memory/store.json with the resolved project root textually, and CPython's Windows realpath keeps the \\?\ extended-length prefix when the file exists at its first lookup but not at its second — another writer atomically replacing the store between the two. Fail-closed: the write is refused, nothing is corrupted, no gate is affected.
